OpenVerifyVersion.name: OpenVerify-Version
OpenVerifyVersion.description: The API version to serve. Without it the API key’s `api-version` applies, and a dashboard user session gets the latest version. A version the API does not support answers 400 `https://openverify.dev/problems/unsupported-api-version`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes the request safe to retry for 24 hours. The same key with the same request replays the stored answer, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The key with another request answers 422 `https://openverify.dev/problems/idempotency-key-reused`; while the first request still runs, 409 `https://openverify.dev/problems/idempotency-key-in-use`. A 5xx answer is not stored, so a retry runs the request again.

OpenVerifyVersion.description: The API version this answer was served with.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed per window by the tightest rate limit that counted this request. The RateLimit headers are absent when the request was not authenticated, or when the limiter is unavailable (it fails open).

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the window of that limit.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until that limit’s window resets.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before sending the request again.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this is the stored answer of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

RateLimited.description: Too Many Requests: 429 `https://openverify.dev/problems/rate-limited`, over the `api` rate limit of the API key or user session. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

UnsupportedApiVersion.description: Bad Request, including 400 `https://openverify.dev/problems/unsupported-api-version` when `OpenVerify-Version` names a version the API does not support.

IdempotencyKeyInUse.description: Conflict: 409 `https://openverify.dev/problems/idempotency-key-in-use` while a request with the same `Idempotency-Key` still runs.

IdempotencyKeyReused.description: Unprocessable Content: 422 `https://openverify.dev/problems/idempotency-key-reused` when the `Idempotency-Key` was used with another request.

C40.3: a selfie pose also sends `capture-id`, `nonce` and `client-elapsed-ms`, before the file; they are required for a selfie verification created since Phase 4 (409 `selfie_capture_required` without them) and refused for the other kinds (400). The pose must be one the capture prompts (422) and the capture `initiated` and unexpired (409 `selfie_capture_invalid`, the same body for a wrong nonce, a foreign, superseded or expired capture). A pose uploaded again replaces the earlier file.

Checks the files the flow step requires, then queues the checks. Repeating it while the verification is `submitted` only queues it again. C40.4: a selfie names its capture (`{ "capture": { "id", "nonce", "device"? } }`), and one created since Phase 4 must (409 `selfie_capture_required`). Every prompted pose needs a file under the capture (409 `selfie_capture_incomplete`); a wrong nonce or a foreign, superseded, consumed or expired capture answers one 409 `selfie_capture_invalid`. The capture is consumed once, with the device snapshot (bounded; the label cleaned and cut to 200 characters) sealed; a repeat must name the capture that submitted the verification. A government ID sends no body or `{}`.

C40.2: a capture with a nonce (returned here once), an expiry (`SELFIE_CAPTURE_TTL_SECONDS` after creation) and the ordered pose prompts, `center` first, the side poses in a random order for active liveness; `guidance` gives the pose thresholds and the hold time. Needs consent and an `initiated` selfie verification; `upload` exists in sandbox environments only (403 `sandbox-only`). A new capture errors the open one (`superseded`, or `expired` past its expiry) and deletes its files. The 11th capture of a verification cancels it instead: 409 `selfie_capture_limit`, after which a new attempt starts (or, with no attempt left, the inquiry has failed).

get.description: Status and user-facing retry hints only, never fraud check details.

post.description: C171.4 (WCAG 2.2.1): moves the open capture's expiry by 180 s. Allowed at least ten times per capture, never counted towards the cap of captures, and refused once the selfie is submitted (409 `selfie_capture_not_extendable`). It answers the capture, without its nonce.

post.summary: Enter the values of a verification
post.description: C52.3: the entered values of a `database`, `aamva` (form source), `database-business` or `business-website` verification, as the body for its type names them (kebab-case, strict). A field the step does not collect is refused and a required one must be present (422 with a JSON Pointer per field). Values are cleaned, capped, sealed and never echoed; a new body replaces earlier values while the verification is `initiated`. Requires consent. The answer is the verification with `inputs-received`.

C55: sends a code to the `phone-number` (a phone verification) or `email-address` (an email verification), validated first (422 `otp_destination_invalid`, `otp_destination_not_allowed`). A send to another destination supersedes the open code. Cooldowns answer 429 `otp_resend_too_soon` with `resend-available-at`; a limit answers 429 `otp_rate_limited` with `Retry-After`, or 503 while the limit store is down; a failed delivery 502 `otp_delivery_failed`; a send after confirmation 409 `otp_already_confirmed`. Requires consent. The answer is the verification with its `guidance.otp` state, never the code.

C55: a correct code moves the verification to `confirmed`. A wrong one answers 422 `otp_incorrect` with `attempts-remaining`; 409 `otp_not_sent`, `otp_expired`, `otp_code_exhausted`, `otp_attempts_exhausted` (the verification was submitted) or `otp_already_confirmed`; 429 `otp_rate_limited` once the destination guess budget tripped, 503 while the limit store is down. Requires consent.

C57.2: the message to sign for `wallet-address` on `chain-id`, returned once with its id and expiry (600 s); a new challenge supersedes the open one. 422 `crypto_chain_not_offered`, `crypto_address_invalid` or `crypto_expected_address_mismatch`; the 11th challenge cancels the verification (a retryable attempt) and answers 409 `crypto_challenge_invalid`. Requires consent.

C62.5: an 8-byte nonce (16 hex characters) for Active Authentication, returned once with its id and expiry (300 s), stored as SHA-256; the 11th challenge cancels the verification (a retryable attempt). Requires consent.

post.summary: Report that this client cannot read a document chip
post.description: C207.9: the client cannot read a document chip (no NFC hardware, no reader installed, NFC off and declined, or a platform that cannot read one). Self-reported, and never a pass: the verification ends `canceled` and the flow takes the `nfc` step’s fallback. Only for the current step of type `nfc`, once per verification (409 `client_unable_not_allowed`).

post.summary: Take a sandbox test chip (sandbox only)
post.description: C208.1: **sandbox environments only** (404 anywhere else). A synthetic chip for the verification’s challenge: its files as base64, every file but DG2, which the server attaches itself (`dg2-attached`), and the Active Authentication response when the scenario’s chip has a key. It proves the flow and the server’s checks, never a reader. 409 `sandbox_chip_anchor_missing` without the sandbox test anchor; 422 `sandbox_chip_scenario_unavailable` for a scenario this server cannot build. 10 an hour per inquiry (`flow-sandbox-chip`).

C94.2: one screen of the collector (or the Android SDK), aggregates and closed vocabularies only. 409 `consent_required` until the session may collect; `recognition` is dropped without its tier; a repeated `sequence` and bodies beyond the 200th answer 202 and are not stored. 60 a minute per session (`flow-signals`).

C211.3: one challenge for the inquiry's Play Integrity token: an `ich_` id, the `request-hash` the device binds its token to, and its expiry (600 s). Only while the session asks for a token (`integrity.request`). 5 an hour per inquiry with the token route (`flow-integrity`).

C211.3: the device's token for the session's open challenge, decoded on the server in a job (never in this request) and judged there; the token is never echoed or logged. 409 `integrity_challenge_invalid` for a challenge unknown, used, expired or another session's. 5 an hour per inquiry with the challenge route (`flow-integrity`).

C238.4: the person’s affirmative act on the `share_consent` step at this position, with the digests of the texts shown (422 `consent_text_mismatch`) and the separate biometric tick when the share carries it (422 `explicit_consent_required`).
C238.1, C236.11: a declined record; the flow continues on the step’s next port.
C237.6: a step listed in `withdrawable-share-consents` (else 409 `flow_step_not_current`); `withdrawn-via: flow`, the same effects as the API’s withdrawal, and the position does not move.

C96.3: a single-use `ovh_` token for the waiting `device_handoff` step, bound to this session; a new one revokes the previous. `qr` answers the fragment the flow draws the QR from; `email` and `sms` send a link to the inquiry’s confirmed destination of that channel (422 `destination_not_confirmed`, unless the step asks for a confirmation code) and answer no token. With `confirmationCode`, the answer carries the six digits the phone types. 5 an hour per session (`flow-handoffs`), 10 an hour per address (`flow-handoffs-ip`); the per-environment send budget fails closed (429 or 503 `handoff_send_limited`).
C96.3 (F01): records `continued_here` for the waiting handoff step where the step allows it (409 `continue_here_not_allowed` otherwise).

post.summary: Decline a handoff on the phone

post.summary: Redeem a handoff on the phone
post.description: C96.3 (P28): no credentials; sent on Continue, never at boot. The token is checked first, in constant time, and every failure answers 410 `handoff_token_invalid` (after 5 wrong codes the token is revoked); only then does the session cap apply (409 `session_limit_reached`). Answers a new session token, which the phone keeps in memory only; the new session starts at the step after the handoff, once it consents. Rate-limited per client address (`one-time-link-redeem`).

C148.5: the values of the current screen step by field key, and the key of the button pressed (absent: the primary button). Only the current step accepts it (409 `flow_step_not_current`); every value is validated again on the server, a hidden component's value is discarded, and the answer is the session at the next step. A resubmission of a step already left answers the current session.
